title: Spanning-tree count as a determinant of stacked bond- and cycle-space basis matrices
statement: Let $G$ be a finite digraph with vertex set $V$ and arc set $A$, and let $T$ be a spanning tree of $G$. Let $B$ be the basis matrix of the bond space $\mathcal{B}$ corresponding to $T$, whose rows are indexed by the arcs of $T$, and let $C$ be the basis matrix of the cycle space $\mathcal{C}$ corresponding to $T$, whose rows are indexed by the arcs not in $T$; both have integer entries and columns indexed by all of $A$. Form the square integer matrix $M$ with rows indexed by $A$ by assigning to each arc of $T$ its row of $B$ and to each remaining arc its row of $C$. Then the number $\tau(G)$ of spanning trees of $G$ satisfies $\tau(G) = \det M$ or $\tau(G) = -\det M$; that is, $\tau(G) = \abs{\det M}$.
hypotheses_covered: T is a spanning tree of the digraph
B is the tree-T basis matrix of the bond space (rows indexed by arcs in T)
C is the tree-T basis matrix of the cycle space (rows indexed by arcs not in T)
B and C have integer entries with columns indexed by all arcs
the square matrix M is formed by stacking B on the arcs of T and C on the complementary arcs
replaced:
\emph{\texttt{$\tau$(G) = $\pm$ det [B; C]}}, the determinant of the square
matrix obtained by stacking a tree-basis matrix of \texttt{$\mathcal{B}$} on top of one
of \texttt{$\mathcal{C}$}.
